Qere without ketiv in near-Aleppo

Features of interest · Interesting ketiv/qere cases · NAEE book links

Qere without ketiv has no letters for the qere written in the body text, though these letters are written in a marginal note. The space and marks in the body text of the manuscript can nevertheless differ.

The verses below show:

  • The page shows the current near-Aleppo example edition (NAEE) contents for the case at hand.
  • The page includes any MAM notes regarding the case at hand.
  • The page includes Aleppo images showing the case at hand.

Image readings are attributed to Ben Denckla.

A masorah circle appears to be present in every case below. Circle presence is noted here once because it does not distinguish the cases or require different supplemental templates. MAM's notes and their complete translations retain their references to circles.

Discrepancies with MAM

  • 2 Samuel 16:23 — MAM calls the space "only a narrow space"; Ben calls it "fairly generous, even after the maqaf", insufficient for the qere letters but ample for its below-marks. The discrepancy concerns the assessment of the space. Both descriptions say that pointing is absent.

Encoding conventions

The intended encoding retains each קרי ולא כתיב call and its qere, and supplements that call with one additional template describing the body text. The supplement records which niqqud are present and whether horizontal space is present. The cases below require three kinds of supplement:

  • For niqqud with horizontal space above the marks, a candidate is ניקוד בלי אות (niqqud without a letter).
  • For niqqud without horizontal space above the marks, a candidate is ניקוד בלי אות ובלי רווח (niqqud without a letter and without space).
  • Horizontal space without niqqud requires a new supplement whose name and syntax remain open.

The phrase “space above the marks” means horizontal space in the line of letters, left between words or at the end of a manuscript line. At a line ending, that horizontal space may have been left on purpose or may be accidental. The end-of-line cases here are Judges 20:13 and Ruth 3:17. None of the cases discussed here is at the start of a manuscript line.

The existing marks templates are specific to near-Aleppo. Their payloads use artificial carrier letters to hold the marks; those carriers are not written manuscript letters. The original convention uses alef carriers. A carrier payload for an unsettled case is left open here.

Current status: every site below still uses קרי ולא כתיב (qere without ketiv). No supplemental template is applied at these sites yet. The supplemental calls' exact names, parameter shapes and placement remain to be designed. Intended supplements are labelled pending, separately from the complete current source notation.

MAM qere

[בְּנֵ֣י]

Current MAM doc-note

Aleppo manuscript reading

The below-marks of בְּנֵ֣י (sheva, tsere, munaḥ) are present without letters, with space above them. There is no dagesh for this qere in the body text, as expected, since dagesh marks are never included there in cases of qere without ketiv. The orphan marks are at the end of a manuscript line. The line ending may have provided space for the marks, possibly accidentally.

MAM qere

[בָּאִ֖ים]

Current MAM doc-note

יָמִ֥ים [בָּאִ֖ים] נְאֻם־יְהֹוָ֑ה =לק ובדפוסים
  • א=הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים [] יְהֹוָֽה (חסר ניקוד ברווח המיועד ל"קרי ולא כתיב")
  • הערת ברויאר
  • קורן, ברויאר, סימנים, מכון ממרא

English translation of the MAM doc-note

MAM's displayed text agrees with the Leningrad Codex, the Cairo Codex of the Prophets, and the printed editions.

  • The Aleppo Codex has the following body text:

    הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים [] יְהֹוָֽה

    Pointing is missing from the space intended for "qere without ketiv".

  • MAM cites Breuer's note.

  • MAM lists Koren, Breuer, the Simanim Tanakh, and Mechon Mamre.

Aleppo manuscript reading

For בָּאִ֖ים, the body text has a rather generous horizontal space between the surrounding written atoms, with no qere letters or niqqud.

The damage to the marginal qere note looks as if opaque tape had been laid parallel to the right margin, obscuring approximately the first letter of each inferred word on its own line. The cause of the damage is unknown. The tape comparison describes how the damage looks; it does not propose a mechanism.

The marginal qere note is inferred to have one word per line:

באים
קרי
ולם
כתב

Comparison with MAM

Agreement: Both descriptions say that pointing is absent at the qere site. Ben additionally describes the generous spacing and damaged marginal note. MAM also gives surrounding text that Ben has not assessed here: its Aleppo illustration omits נְאֻם־ and has יְהֹוָֽה. Those additional MAM statements do not establish a disagreement with Ben.
